svg.text: SYSTEM DESIGN BLUEPRINT - PRINCIPAL ENGINEER INTERVIEW CHEAT SHEET
Flow of the interview: Requirements > Estimates > API > Data model > High-level design > Deep dive > Failures > Trade-offs > Evolution
Chips = datastore the service talks to:
Web / mobile app. Retries with backoff + jitter, Idempotency-Key on writes, uploads
media straight to S3 with a presigned URL.
GeoDNS / Anycast: route to nearest healthy region
WAF: DDoS, bot and OWASP rules, IP reputation
AuthN: JWT / OAuth2 (short-lived access + refresh, revocation list)
AuthZ / scopes; mTLS to upstream services
Rate limiting: HTTP 429 + Retry-After (token bucket, Redis + Lua)
Timeouts + circuit breaker per upstream; stateless, scales horizontally
Say: gateway = cross-cutting concerns only, NO business logic
RoundRobin, Weighted RR, Hashing, Least Connections (WebSocket: least-conn)
L4 (TCP / WS, fastest) vs L7 (path / host routing, TLS, header rules, more CPU)
Health checks (active + passive), connection draining on deploy
Multi-AZ; LB pair itself redundant (no SPOF); consistent hashing for cache locality
Service discovery (K8s DNS / Consul), client-side load balancing
mTLS between services; retries / timeouts / circuit-breaking as sidecar policy
Central config + feature flags (kill switch, gradual rollout)
Source of truth: Postgres (ACID, unique email / username)
Redis: profile + session cache (cache-aside, TTL); passwords hashed (argon2 /
Read replicas first; shard by user_id only when needed
Owns follow graph; emits UserCreated / UserDeleted (GDPR) events
Redis caches member lists of hot groups
Cap group size / paginate members; owns 'who is in this group' for fan-out
Owns the live TCP / WebSocket connection (stateful, per node)
In-memory MAP <userId, WebSocketConnection> e.g. MAP<AMIT, conn>
Auth on upgrade (JWT); ping / pong heartbeat; reconnect with backoff + resume
Tens of thousands of conns per node (tune ulimit / epoll); least-conn LB
Graceful drain on deploy: clients reconnect to another node
Connection registry in Redis: user > WSH node (TTL refreshed by heartbeat)
Example: WSH1 > [ATUL, AMIT] and AMIT > WSH1
Routes a message to the right WSH (Redis pub/sub or internal gRPC)
No registry entry = user offline > Notification Service (APNs / FCM)
Node crash: stale entries expire via TTL; reconnect re-registers
Resolves group members (Group Service + Redis cache) and fans out
Small groups: fan-out on write per member; huge groups: pull / batched delivery
Ordering: Kafka partition key = conversation_id / group_id
Delivery states: sent > delivered > read (acks, retries, dedupe by msg_id)
Idempotent writes by client msg_id (safe retries)
Offline sync: fetch since last_msg_id (cursor), not offset
E2E encryption (Signal-style) if required; TTL for disappearing messages
Search over messages: index separately in Elasticsearch
Heartbeat > Redis key with TTL (online = key exists)
Publish presence only to friends / open chats (avoid fan-out storms)
STUN: peer discovers its public IP:port (NAT mapping) so it can connect directly
TURN: relays media when direct P2P fails (symmetric NAT / firewalls); costs
ICE order: host > STUN > TURN; signalling over WebSocket
Group calls: SFU (not mesh); 1:1 calls: P2P
Saga, ACID, CAP / PACELC, Consistent Hashing, Bloom Filter, Pagination, Partitioning, Sharding, Replication
Circuit breaker, bulkhead, retry with exponential backoff + jitter, timeouts, load shedding
Distributed tracing with CorrelationIds; SLI / SLO / error budget; alert on symptoms
Payments = CP | Feed = AP | Inventory = strong consistency with a reservation TTL
Deployments (canary, blue-green, feature flags), schema migrations without downtime (expand > contract),
'I chose X because the requirement is Y. The cost is Z, mitigated by M, and I'd revisit if <trigger>.'
Delivers content closer to the user (edge PoPs)
Push CDN vs Pull CDN (pull = long tail, push = known-hot / launch)
Origin server vs edge server; origin shield cuts origin load
Lower latency, reduced origin load, better scalability, security, resilience
CloudFront; cache key + TTL; prefer versioned URLs over invalidation
Signed URLs / cookies for private media
S3 event > Kafka > async transcoding / moderation
Blob in S3; metadata (owner, size, status) in Postgres
Chunked / resumable upload; virus + NSFW content filter
Auto-tag (ML); transcode to multiple bitrates (HLS) + thumbnails
Async Kafka workers; status pending > processed > published
Used by Post Ingestion, Message Service, Orders:
Guard clock skew; workerId via etcd / ZooKeeper lease
Query path: LB > Search Service > Elasticsearch
Autocomplete: edge-ngram / prefix; cache hot queries (Redis / CDN)
Pagination: search_after cursor, never deep offset
Timeout + fallback (cached / degraded results) if ES is slow
1. Full Text Search, Fuzzy Search; supports filtering, ranking and
NOT the source of truth: rebuild via reindex (alias swap) from
Primary shard count is fixed at index creation: plan growth
Consumes post / asset events from Kafka and bulk-indexes into ES
Idempotent upsert by doc id + version; poison messages > DLQ
Postgres: orders as a state machine (ACID)
Redis lock (SET NX EX 300) against double booking is an
optimisation; the guarantee is a DB unique constraint /
MongoDB: stock per SKU; atomic conditional update
Reservation with TTL: released if payment fails
Consumes reserve / release events from Kafka
Oversell guard: strong consistency (w: majority). Be ready
Create order > Reserve stock > Charge payment > Confirm
Any step fails > compensate: release stock, refund
Saga over 2PC: no distributed locks, stays available; cost = temporary inconsistency +
Orchestration for checkout (visible flow); choreography for simple event chains
Idempotency key with unique index: no double charge on
PSP calls with retries + webhooks; reconcile nightly; never
Outbox row is written in the SAME DB transaction as the
order; Debezium tails the WAL and publishes to Kafka
Fixes dual-write; at-least-once so consumers must be
Validate, dedupe (Idempotency-Key), assign Snowflake post_id; return fast (201 / 202)
Write post to Cassandra, publish PostCreated to Kafka (key = author_id); fan-out, search and analytics run
Dual-write risk between Cassandra and Kafka > outbox / CDC, or Kafka-first and persist from a consumer
High write throughput (LSM tree: commit log > memtable > SSTable)
Predictable access pattern: one table per query
Consistent hashing ring + virtual nodes; Gossip protocol
Tunable consistency (R + W > N; RF = 3, LOCAL_QUORUM)
Wide Column database; Bloom filter per SSTable skips disk reads
Tombstones and compaction strategies; time-bucket keys to avoid unbounded partitions
Say: PK = user_id (+ bucket), clustering = post_id DESC; no joins / ad-hoc queries
FanOut on READ: famous / passive users
Active users: timeline = Redis ZSET of post_ids (O(1)
read), hydrate bodies via Post Service (Cassandra)
Famous / passive users: fan-out on READ, pull + merge at
HYBRID: push for ordinary users, pull for celebrities, rank
Cursor pagination; cache only active users' timelines
Cache, RateLimiter, Distributed Lock, Counter, LeaderBoard
CacheConsistency: invalidation, short TTL, eventual consistency
HotKeys: replicate hot keys, application (local) cache, rate limiter
Kafka consumer (post.created): for each follower of an ordinary author, ZADD
post_id into that follower's Redis timeline
Group posts: resolve members via Group Service, then same fan-out
ZADD is idempotent: safe on replay; failures > retry topic > DLQ
Celebrity posts skipped: pulled at read time
In-memory database; crash recovery with RDB snapshots and AOF log; single-threaded command execution (atomic ops)
Cluster mode: 16,384 hash slots; replicas + failover (Sentinel / Cluster); eviction LRU / LFU; maxmemory
SET key value NX EX 300 = lock primitive. Limits: expiry mid-work, failover loses lock > use fencing tokens; the DB constraint is the real guarantee
Kafka is a log, not a queue:
Every service emits metrics + logs + traces via OpenTelemetry SDK (traceparent / correlation-id propagated)
Metrics > Prometheus, Logs > Loki / ELK, Traces > Tempo / Jaeger, all visualised in Grafana
RED / USE dashboards, SLI > SLO > error budget; alert on symptoms (burn rate), not causes; tail-based trace sampling
Consumes notif.events; dedupes (Redis), honours user prefs / quiet hours (Postgres)
Channel order: WebSocket (online) > APNs / FCM push (offline) > email / SMS; collapse keys
Retry with backoff, DLQ, per-user rate limit; at-least-once + idempotency key = no duplicate pushes
Ingests external / partner / warehouse feeds (batch + stream) into Kafka
Validates + normalises, idempotent producer, schema registry; bad records > DLQ; backpressure
Partner auth (mTLS / API key) + per-partner rate limits
Consumes view / like / follow events from Kafka
Offline: batch ML builds candidate sets; online: ANN vector lookup + ranking; features in Redis / feature store
Cache results per user; cold start > popularity fallback; A/B tests behind feature flags
Stream jobs (Flink / Spark) compute counters, DAU, funnels; replay Kafka for backfills
Hot counters in Redis (INCR) flushed in batches; HyperLogLog for uniques, Count-Min for top-K
Kappa / lambda trade-off: one pipeline vs separate batch + stream
Looks up user > WSH node in the Redis registry and delivers via Web Socket Manager (see section 3)
Only connected users; others fall back to Notification Service push
Ordering per conversation; ack + retry; dedupe by msg_id
Say the mitigation, not just the failure
Redis down: fall back to DB with request coalescing; replicas + failover; protect the DB from a stampede
Kafka broker down: acks=all + min.insync.replicas keep data; producers retry; outbox buffers writes
Consumer lag: scale consumers (up to partition count), shed non-critical work, alert on lag
Cassandra node down: RF=3 + LOCAL_QUORUM still serves; hinted handoff + repair
Postgres primary down: promote a replica (know RPO / RTO); read replicas keep serving reads
WebSocket node down: clients reconnect (backoff + jitter); registry TTL expires; offline users get push
Elasticsearch behind / down: serve cached or degraded results; reindex from Kafka
Slow dependency (the usual culprit): timeouts, circuit breaker, bulkhead, load shedding
Retry storm / thundering herd: exponential backoff + jitter, request coalescing, rate limits
Poison message: retry topic > DLQ with alert + replay tool
Region outage: GeoDNS failover; active-active vs active-passive chosen from RPO / RTO
Hot partition / hot key: bucketed keys, key salting, replicate hot keys, local cache
Requirements first (functional + non-functional), then estimates: QPS, storage / day, bandwidth, read:write ratio, cache size
API design (REST / gRPC), idempotent writes, cursor pagination, versioning; data model + access patterns BEFORE choosing the DB
OAuth2 / JWT (short-lived), refresh rotation, mTLS inside, encryption in transit + at rest (KMS), secrets in Vault
PII / GDPR: data minimisation, delete pipeline (UserDeleted event), audit logs, abuse + DDoS protection
Active-active vs active-passive; define RPO / RTO; GeoDNS / Anycast
Cassandra multi-DC, Kafka MirrorMaker, S3 cross-region replication; conflicts: last-write-wins or CRDT
Trade-off + trigger to revisit; cost awareness (storage tiering, CDN egress, Redis memory)
Evolution: modular monolith first, split services when team size / scale demands it; build vs buy; team boundaries (Conway)
SERVICE > DATASTORE MAP (which service talks to which DB)
Atomic counters via Lua; decide fail-open vs fail-closed
Per node; lost on crash, so client reconnects
Fast lookup; TTL clears stale nodes
Full-text; never the source of truth
High write; outbox / CDC closes the dual-write gap
Fan-out on write for ordinary users
